findings.description: The kickoff now hard-codes `subagent_type: "security-reviewer"`, an agent that exists only in pupitre's own `.claude/agents/`; nothing in `src/` installs it, so in an adopted repo the conductor's pre-gate security review spawns an unknown (or unrelated) agent, where the previous general-purpose subagent worked everywhere.
findings.body:
**The conductor's security review now depends on an agent that exists only in pupitre's own checkout**

[`profile-compiler.service.ts#L964-L978`](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/645af1f36dfde17ecd5a17c54515d35441bdf66e/src/core/profile-compiler.service.ts#L964-L978) has the conductor call the Agent tool with `subagent_type: "security-reviewer"`. That agent is defined only in `.claude/agents/security-reviewer.md` in this repo. Nothing in `src/` installs it: the only `.claude/agents` reference is the comment at L995. The package ships only `bin`, and the conductor launch passes `--setting-sources user` with no `--agents` or plugin dir (`src/claude/session-runtime.service.ts:692-693`).

The conductor runs in whatever repo was registered with `pup init` (`launchConductor` uses `cwd: opts.repoPath`, `src/claude/session-runtime.service.ts:922-939`), and the README says adopting Pupitre commits nothing to that repo. The bullet has no repo-specific condition. It fires on any session diff touching a `CRITICAL_AREAS` entry, including the generic `.github/**` (`src/core/routing.utils.ts:21`), or on a task set to `--tier critical`. So in an adopted repo:

- **No `security-reviewer` agent:** the spawn fails, and the pre-gate review is skipped or improvised.
- **An unrelated `security-reviewer` agent:** the prompt goes to an agent that may lack Bash or this protocol. The pupitre manifest itself is written for pupitre's internals (`gateChildEnv`, decision 29, `docs/adr/`).

Before this PR, a general-purpose subagent worked in every repo. ADR 0118 doesn't address non-pupitre repos.

Suggested fix (pick one):
- Have pup supply the agent itself, for example as `--agents` JSON or as an agent file written into the conductor's compiled profile.
- Make the bullet conditional: use `security-reviewer` when it exists in the main checkout, and otherwise fall back to a general-purpose subagent carrying the same rules.

Then record the chosen scope in ADR 0118.

findings.description: Claude Code cuts long Bash output (about 30k characters), and the "no other git" rule leaves the reviewer no allowed way to page past the cut (no pathspec, no `--stat`). A session can push its critical hunk past it by padding the diff with earlier-sorting files or by setting the unpinned `diff.orderFile`. A coverage loss, not a gate bypass: consider allowing the pinned command with `-c diff.orderFile=` and an optional `-- ':(literal)<path>'`.

The diff is pinned to `refs/heads/pup/<session-id>` because the session can move its worktree HEAD (decision 80), but context reads are told to use Read under `.worktrees/<session-id>/`. Those files can come from a different commit than the one under review, so a session can shape what the reviewer sees around its hunks.

`model: "opus"` is inlined as a literal while the effort comes from `SECURITY_REVIEW_EFFORT`, so only half of the model/effort pair is a constant (docs/conventions/general.md §No hardcoded values). A `SECURITY_REVIEW_MODEL` next to the effort constant would keep the pair together.

`SECURITY_REVIEW_TURNS` (a threshold) and `SECURITY_REVIEWER_AGENT` (an agent name) are module-private consts with `//` comments, not named exports with JSDoc in a `*.constants.ts` (docs/conventions/general.md §No hardcoded values). They are also split from `SECURITY_REVIEW_EFFORT` in `src/claude/model-ladder.constants.ts`.

The comment on `SECURITY_REVIEWER_AGENT` ("The project agent in `.claude/agents/`, which carries the review protocol and its own effort") mostly narrates what the name refers to, which ADR 0118 already explains. Delete it or cut it to the one non-obvious fact.

The Security review bullet is one long semicolon-chained sentence. It never numbers the "four rules" the ADR names, "Its prompt hands it" has an ambiguous antecedent, and "report within 10 turns, reading only the files around a hunk it needs" mixes the turn cap with the read rule.

The new test pins long verbatim prompt fragments, including a 3-line clause-spanning literal ending in incidental wording ("runs the diff drivers"), so any rewording breaks it even when the rules are unchanged. Assert only the load-bearing rule phrases.

Protocol step 2 still has the conductor run `git -C .worktrees/<session-id> log --oneline main..HEAD` with bare `main`/`HEAD` and without `--no-replace-objects` or `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`. That is exactly the pattern the rewritten security bullet warns against (decisions 41 and 80), so the two now contradict each other in the same prompt.
